baseline.about: What ships: steady sampling, examples, argument repair, the claim check, forced follow-up, reply as a tool on the first round.

no-harness.about: The model on its own: default sampling, no examples, no repair, no claim check, no forced follow-up.

warm.about: Like baseline, but sampled at the server's usual temperature.

no-examples.about: Like baseline, without the worked examples (saves tokens).

old-prompt.about: Like baseline, with the 0.15 system prompt (before the Home Assistant/Cline-style rules).
old-prompt.system_prompt: You are the user's assistant, running locally on the user's laptop (Fedora Silverblue with GNOME) on its NPU. Be brief and direct. When the user asks you to do something on the computer, or asks about its state, call a tool instead of describing how to do it. Only call tools the request needs. Connect the dots: work out what the user means from the conversation, what you remember about them and what's on the computer ("my phone" is the device they told you about, "it" is what you just made or found), and pass one tool's result to the next. After looking something up to do a task, go on and do the task. If a tool fails, fix the call and try again, or look the options up first; say what failed only when you can't work it out. Never invent tool results. Answer in the user's language.

no-context.about: Like baseline, without the list of devices and networks in the prompt.

no-forcing.about: Like baseline, without re-asking with only the finishing tools after a lookup.

reply-tool.about: Same as baseline (reply as a tool is on by default since 0.17).

no-reply-tool.about: Like baseline, but the model may answer in plain text on the first round (0.16.1 and before).

compact.about: Like baseline, with ~28 broad tools (set, connect, send, find, read, calendar…) all sent every time instead of 64 routed narrow ones.

prompt-0.18.about: Like baseline, with the 0.18.0 prompts (system prompt, web, memory, escalate, nudge) before the 0.18.1 rewrite.
prompt-0.18.system_prompt:
You are the user's assistant, running locally on their laptop (Fedora Silverblue with GNOME) on its NPU. Be brief and direct, and answer in the user's language.
To do something on the computer, or to find out anything about it, call a tool. You can check and change things, so never say you can't when a tool covers it, and never say something is done unless a tool did it. A reply without a tool call ends your turn: if something still needs doing, call the tool now instead of saying you will. For chat and general knowledge, just answer, without tools.
Connect the dots: work out what the user means from the chat, what you remember about them, and what's on this computer (listed below). "My phone" is the device they told you about or the phone in the list, "it" is what you just made or found. Use names as the user said them or as listed. If several things fit and you can't tell which, ask; if one fits, use it. Pass one tool's result to the next, and after looking something up for a task, go on and do the task. If a tool fails, fix the call and try again, or look the options up; say what failed only when you can't work it out. Never invent tool results.

prompt_parts.web: For anything recent or that you aren't sure of, use web_search and read the most relevant result with read_web_page, then answer briefly and name the source.
prompt_parts.memory: When the user tells you a lasting preference or fact about themselves, or asks you to remember something, call remember. Use what you remember without mentioning it.
prompt_parts.escalate: If a request needs more than you can do well (careful reasoning, longer writing, code, several steps, or you're unsure), call ask_smarter_model instead of guessing. It hands the task to a bigger local model, which answers the user directly.
prompt_parts.nudge: (You said it's done, but no tool ran, so nothing happened yet. Call the tool now to do it, or say plainly that you can't.)

required.about: Like baseline, but every round must call exactly one tool, reply and ask_user always offered (redesign step 2).

compact-required.about: The compact tool set, every round one required call: the redesign's fixed toolbox.

no-embed.about: Like baseline, routing by keywords only (no embedding model).

examples.about: Like baseline, but meaning picks tool groups from the nearest example requests (tools/requests.tsv) instead of the group descriptions (redesign step 1).

examples-force.about: Like examples, and when the nearest examples clearly agree on one tool, the first round offers only it (with reply and ask_user).

examples-only.about: Like examples, without the keyword lists (redesign step 3).

examples-force-only.about: Like examples-force, without the keyword lists.

pre-cues.about: Like baseline, with the tool descriptions from before the Polish cue words (0.29): set_volume, set_brightness, media_control, open_file.

descriptions.set_volume: Set the output volume in percent (0-100).
descriptions.set_brightness: Set the screen brightness in percent (1-100).
descriptions.media_control: Control music and video players: play, pause, play_pause, next_track (skip this song), previous_track (go back a song), stop, or status (only to say what's playing).
descriptions.open_file: Open a file or folder with its default app. Paths can be relative to the home folder, start with ~, or start with a folder name like Downloads or Documents.

all-tools.about: Every tool with every request, in the same order (no routing, no embedding model), 16K context: the server reuses the prompt it read for the next question.

all-tools-short.about: Like all-tools, with shorter descriptions for the ten longest tools.

descriptions.research: Research a topic in depth on the web and write a report with sections and cited sources, shown as it is (a few minutes; "quick research" reads 5 pages, under a minute). Use it when the user asks to research, look into, review or compare something; for one quick fact use web_search. save_as pdf, md or txt saves it in Documents/Research.
descriptions.rewrite_selection: Rewrite the text the user selected in any app (proofread, shorten, make formal, translate); the result goes to the clipboard. Use it for "this", "the selected text", "popraw to". It reads the selection itself, so don't ask for the text.
descriptions.search_everything: Search all the user's own things at once (calendar, mail, file names and contents, contacts) when you can't tell where the answer is ("when's my flight?", "what did the landlord say?"). query: key words, not a sentence.
descriptions.write_file: Create a text file (note, list, script, letter…) with the given content; a path ending in .pdf makes a PDF from Markdown. To change an existing file use edit_file; overwrite true replaces a whole file.
descriptions.open_app: Open an app. If the user names one ('Firefox', 'Zed'), pass that exact name, even if misspelled; otherwise pass the kind (browser, email, files, calendar, music, video, photos, text editor, pdf, terminal, settings) for their default.
descriptions.send_text: Send a text note (an answer, list, address, link) to one of the user's devices with Taildrop; for the last answer, pass its text. For files use send_file.
descriptions.read_file: Read any file's text (notes, code, CSV, PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, LibreOffice, EPUB, e-mail…). Long files come in parts: pass from_line to read on. For a question about a long document, use ask_document.
descriptions.web_search: Search the web for current facts, news, prices or how-tos; returns titles, links and snippets. Not for the user's own files, settings or devices. To research or look into something, use research.
descriptions.search_mail: Search the user's mail (all accounts, any mail app) by sender, subject or topic; returns the newest matches with sender, subject, date and the start of the text. Empty query: the newest mail.
descriptions.find_files: Find the user's files and folders by part of their name, newest first. Use it whenever they mention one of their documents ("my lease", "the invoice", "my CV") to read or send it.
